newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: HEINEKEN SHARES SURGE ON EARNINGS SPECULATION.
newsitem.headline: HEINEKEN SHARES SURGE ON EARNINGS SPECULATION.

text.p: Shares in Heineken surged over three percent or 11.00 guilders on Wednesday, fuelled by newspaper reports over earnings prospects at the Dutch brewer.
Dutch daily De Telegraaf said Board member Johan Drost was reported as saying 1996 earnings would at least equal those of 1995, when speaking at the World Economic Forum in Davos.
Heineken was not available for comment on Wednesday, but the paper said the company had denied any such statement.
But dealers said the stock was back in favour on the market.
"There are a lot of Swiss investors who are very keen on Heineken," one said.
Another dealer said demand was widespread, with sellers, recently predominant, becoming rare.
Talk of possible Heineken interest in Israeli brewer Tempo was also boosting the shares, traders said.
"They deny they are having talks on it, just as usual. But Tempo would be very interesting to them," one said.

"And there may be short-covering by those who expected the share to drop to 250 guilders," one dealer suggested. The shares stood at 308.50 at 1230 GMT. -- Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000, Fax +31 20 504 5040
